Beállítom Baka András köztársasági elnöki jelölésére a Fidesz frakcióvezetője is gyorsan reagált. Bóka János a bejegyzésében azt írta, mivel Sulyok Tamás köztársasági elnök megbízatását a Tisza Párt „önkényesen és illegitim módon szüntette meg”, az új köztársasági elnök választását is illegitimnek tartják. „A szappanoperává dagadó jelölési és választási színjátékhoz nem asszisztálunk, a Fidesz frakció a jelölési és választási eljárásban nem vesz részt. Magyarország utolsó legitim köztársasági elnökét Sulyok Tamásnak hívják.” Bóka szerint Baka jogtudósként egy jogsértő eljárásban vesz részt jelenleg és hozzájárul a „Magyar Péter önkényének kiépítéséhez”. Majd felidézte – bár a konkrét esetet nem nevezte meg –, hogy a Legfelsőbb Bíróság akkori elnökeként Magyarországot perelte be a nemzetközi fórumon, Bóka szerint „lényegesen kisebb sérelemért, mint amivel most a köztársasági elnöki tisztség megüresedését a Tisza előidézte”. Bóka itt vélhetően arra utal, amikor Baka András 2016-ban jogerősen pert nyert az Emberi Jogok Legfelsőbb Bíróságán, amely megállapította, hogy személyre szabott jogalkotással menesztették a tisztségéből, mert nyilvánosan kritizálta a bíróságok függetlenségét veszélyeztető lépéseket. A Fidesz frakcióvezetője végül egy jóslatot is tett, és azt írta: „Baka András a funkcióját csak addig fogja betölteni, amíg Magyar Péter egy kommenttel le nem váltja.” Kedvenceink Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! https://www.foreignpolicyjournal.com/202.text: Romania’s Cernavoda Nuclear Plant Goes Offline As Danube Drought Forces Hungary To Dam Europe’s Second-Longest River By Ewan Scott | Aug 14, 2026 | Economy & Business , Energy , Featured , News & Analysis , Politics Romania has shut down its only nuclear power plant after record-low water levels on the Danube River eliminated the facility’s sole cooling water source. The Cernavoda plant, operated by Nuclearelectrica, typically generates around one-fifth of Romania’s electricity under normal operating conditions. This is only the second time the plant has been shut down, with the first closure occurring in 2023 under nearly identical drought and heat conditions. Nuclearelectrica had already taken the step of closing one of Cernavoda’s two reactors last month before conditions forced the final shutdown. On Thursday, the company announced it was shutting the second reactor “because of the significant and ongoing drop in the water level of the Danube River.” Earlier this month, the company enlisted help from Romania’s Navy in a dramatic attempt to keep the plant operational by blowing up a rocky outcrop exposed by the low water levels. The displaced rocks were strategically placed on the riverbed in an effort to redirect more water flow toward the plant’s cooling intake system. Despite these efforts, continued dry weather and falling water levels ultimately made a full shutdown unavoidable for the facility. Plant director Romeo Urjan told AFP that “we do not foresee a restart within the next 10 days,” signaling an extended outage with no immediate relief in sight. Romania’s Energy Ministry said it was sourcing alternative power through wind energy and imports, while warning that large industrial users could face restrictions during evening hours as a last resort. Carmakers Ford and Dacia have already committed to pausing production until August 19 in order to reduce demand on Romania’s strained electricity grid. Across the border in Hungary, Prime Minister Peter Magyar visited the Paks nuclear facility on Thursday, which faces an equally severe threat from the same Danube drought conditions. Magyar told reporters at the site, located roughly 100 kilometers south of Budapest, that “we have begun construction of the low weir that will permanently contribute to raising the Danube’s water level.” Currently, only one of Paks’ four reactors remains operational, a dramatic reduction from the plant’s usual role supplying around half of Hungary’s electricity generation. Nine days ago, Paks came within a razor-thin margin of complete shutdown, with the government only averting that outcome after the Danube’s levels came in a few millimeters higher than forecast. Under normal conditions, the Paks facility accounts for roughly one-third of Hungary’s total electricity consumption, making its continued operation a matter of national energy security. Before the weir is finished, authorities plan to deliberately sink two 80-meter-long barges, placed end-to-end and perpendicular to the river’s flow, to create an initial damming effect. Magyar said Hungarian soldiers are working around the clock on the weir construction and that it should be completed within the next four weeks, raising water levels in front of the plant’s cooling system by more than a meter. The project may be completed just as summer rainfall returns, but low water levels have created a rare window to undertake such river construction work relatively cheaply and efficiently. http://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article.text: More than 60 draft dodgers have been arrested at border crossings since Sunday, many of them haredi (ultra-Orthodox) men attempting to travel to Uman ahead of Rosh Hashanah. Most of the arrests took place at Ben-Gurion Airport as the men attempted to leave Israel, while additional arrests were recorded at the Taba border crossing. The IDF confirmed that dozens of draft dodgers were arrested at border crossings over the past two days but did not provide an exact number or details about the detainees. According to the military, enforcement is carried out routinely in coordination with the Population and Immigration Authority, and preparations for arrests of those who have failed to report for enlistment are adjusted based on situation assessments.The IDF emphasized that those required to enlist can regularize their status and report for service.The “I Entrusted Guards” hotline has meanwhile issued a warning to haredi youths at risk of arrest, urging them to avoid arriving at border crossings. The hotline warned that the risk is not limited to Ben-Gurion Airport and that attempts to leave Israel through land border crossings could also result in arrest.The hotline claimed that young men who had already attempted to leave the country were arrested and transferred to military prison, warning that some could remain imprisoned during Rosh Hashanah. The warning comes as police continue preparations for increased activity at border crossings ahead of the annual wave of travel to Uman.Pilgrimage has become an especially sensitive issue Every year, tens of thousands of Breslov Hasidim from Israel and around the world travel to Uman, Ukraine, to pray at the grave of Rabbi Nachman of Breslov. This year, amid enforcement against draft dodgers, the pilgrimage has become an especially sensitive issue within the community.Senior Breslov rabbis called on those who could face arrest not to arrive at Ben-Gurion Airport and not to attempt to resolve their status solely for the purpose of taking the flight. At the same time, an unofficial initiative has emerged within the community to hold Rosh Hashanah prayers in military prison if the trip cannot take place, in an attempt to create public and operational pressure on the IDF. 'I am willing to sacrifice my life for this'A Breslov Hasid in his 50s who is in Uman with five of his sons told Walla: “There are boys who have been traveling every year since they were five years old. For them, getting to Uman is in their soul.”He said some young men are following the rabbis' instructions and will remain in Israel, while others say that they are “willing to sacrifice their lives for this.”He described attempts to leave through various border crossings, including Egypt and Jordan, based on the assumption that screening there is less predictable. “Everyone has their own ideas. It is a game of cat and mouse,” he said.One of his sons, 24, remained in Israel due to his military status, while two of his other sons serve in the IDF.Military Police activity is carried out in cooperation with the Population and Immigration Authority and according to situation assessments. Enforcement takes place routinely, but forces have been reinforced ahead of the holiday.Those who have been absent from service for a significant period are generally brought before a military court judge, and some are imprisoned. The IDF did not provide a figure for how many of those arrested were transferred to prison.A Population and Immigration Authority official explained that the authority handles anyone who appears in the system as subject to a travel restriction, without knowing in advance the source of the order.“If it is a military order, the army is called to the scene, and it decides whether to arrest [the person],” the official said.According to the official, a technological change implemented during Passover now allows authorities to identify people with travel restrictions during check-in, even when the process is carried out online.A 19-year-old traveling from Poland to Uman told Walla that the arrests have become the main topic of conversation among travelers.“Dozens of young men are not a drop in the ocean. It is probably most of the draft dodgers who were supposed to arrive,” he estimated.
